_comment: DATA-DRIVEN runner disk-reclaim policy (FRIC-017 productization, pipeline-glue(b), ADR-0548 pipeline-as-product). The Rust-first preflight binary oya-cloud-ci-runner-disk-reclaim reads this file for callers that explicitly request a runner profile, best-effort removes the listed vendor preinstall dirs, and asserts the configured post-reclaim free-disk floor. It replaced two duplicated inline sudo rm -rf blocks. ADR-0554 D10 removed the required workflow's owned-runner invocations together with the unsafe whole-tree buck-out restore they existed to precede; this policy remains a reusable hosted-runner capability and a tested attribution contract, not an active required-CI step.

github-hosted-ubuntu-latest._comment: GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest carries ~25-30 GiB of .NET/Android/GHC/CodeQL vendor preinstall on a runner with only ~14 GiB free on /. The buck-out warm restore decompresses a ~5.78 GiB blob (~12-15 GiB on disk) on top of a fetch-depth:0 monorepo checkout, exhausting / (FRIC-017: 'No space left on device' at restore, before any build ran). The 5 dirs are the vendor preinstall trees removed by the retired inline shell.

oya-owned-arc-pod._comment: RETIRED REQUIRED-WORKFLOW PROFILE (owned ARC pod on Talos, runs-on: oya-arm64). Empty reclaim_dirs and a zero floor remain as historical compatibility for explicit callers and tests, but required CI no longer invokes this profile after ADR-0554 D10. An ARC runner image contains none of the hosted profile's vendor preinstalls, and statvfs inside the pod observes the shared node filesystem rather than a trustworthy per-pod expansion budget. The 2026-08-01 incident proved this no-op cannot protect whole buck-out archive extraction: kubelet node-pressure eviction terminated both consumers. Do not treat this profile as a capacity guard or replace zero with an invented node floor.
